discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: The University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the 'magic wavelength' optical lattice, in which neutral atoms are trapped without perturbing their clock transition, uniting the long interrogation of trapped ions with the huge signal of many atoms. He demonstrated the first lattice clocks with strontium, and the scheme was soon extended to ytterbium and other species. Ye brought the concept to unprecedented stability and accuracy, reaching the 10^-18 level and beyond, resolving gravitational redshift over millimetre heights and exploring many-body effects in the clock ensemble. Optical lattice clocks now outperform the caesium standard by two orders of magnitude, drive the planned redefinition of the SI second, enable relativistic geodesy, and serve as tabletop probes of dark matter, variation of fundamental constants and new forces. This invention opened an entire platform used by laboratories worldwide, including ours.
